subject: North Shore Insurance — Hosted API: data lifecycle, residency & deletion commitments
messages:
From: Karen Lopez <karen.lopez@northshoreins.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: security@northshoreins.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0500
Subject: Security questionnaire — quick clarification on residency & retention for Hosted API

Rafael / Laura —

Thanks for taking this. Our security team had two outstanding items on the Hosted API side before procurement signs the SOW:

1) Data residency: can you confirm where request/response data and logs are stored for the Hosted API (region/physical location)? Are we guaranteed to keep data within the US unless otherwise contracted?

2) Retention & deletion: what are your default retention windows for requests, logs, and model outputs? Please describe the deletion workflow (console/API initiation, timelines to purge, and backups).

3) Legal hold / eDiscovery: if we need a preservation hold for a subset of tenant data, how is that handled and how does it interact with your deletion windows?

4) Evidence: can you provide the SOC2 report & a short data flow diagram showing retention points?

Our target is to have a formal answer and any supporting artifacts by COB Thursday so legal can include clauses in the DPA. Let me know if you need an extension.

Appreciate it —
Karen
Security Manager, North Shore Insurance
security@northshoreins.com

(Attachment: NSI_Security_Questionnaire_v3.docx)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Lopez <karen.lopez@northshoreins.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire — quick clarification on residency & retention for Hosted API

Karen —

Thanks for the clear ask. Below are concise responses and the artifacts you requested; attaching a short PDF with the same content for your legal team. If you need an explicit contractual commitment (e.g., limit to US-only storage) we can include geo-binding clauses in the DPA — happy to add that language.

Summary answers (hosted API):

- Residency: default tenant data for the Hosted API is stored in the region you select at onboarding. For North Shore we will pin all production tenant data to the US-East (N. Virginia) and US-West (Oregon) regions only. We will not replicate tenant data to EU/APAC without written instruction.

- Encryption: All data in transit is protected with TLS 1.3. Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. Keys are stored in Redwood-managed HSM-backed KMS for Hosted customers. For enterprise contracts we offer a Private deployment option with customer-managed KMS (BYOK).

- Default retention windows: request and model output artifacts (including request body, generated tokens, and minimal debug logs) are retained for 30 days by default. Short system logs (metrics, infra traces) are kept for 90 days. Audit logs (authn/authz events) are retained for 365 days. These defaults are configurable in contract to 0 / 7 / 30 / 90 / 365 days depending on the tier.

- Deletion workflow:
  * Customer-initiated purge: You can delete specific request records or purge a tenant via the Redwood Console or the Admin API (DELETE /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/data).
  * Primary data purge timeline: items marked for deletion are removed from primary storage within 24 hours (business hours).
  * Backup removal timeline: backups are retained for disaster recovery and then rotated. Deleted tenant data is removed from backups within the configured backup retention window — standard is 90 days. We can negotiate a shorter backup retention in the DPA where operationally feasible; shorter windows may incur operational constraints and a small SLA credit.

- Legal hold / eDiscovery: Redwood can apply a preservation hold on a tenant or a filtered subset (by data tag) upon a valid legal request issued via your admin contact and the legal channel. While on hold, automated deletions are paused for the affected objects. Holds must be requested in writing. Large-scale preservation requests may require a small operational fee for extended storage.

- Evidence & artifacts: attaching our SOC2 Type II package and a simple data flow diagram showing where data is stored and retained. Links: https://drive.redwood.com/reports/SOC2-Q3-2026 (SOC2) and data_flow_diagram_nshore.png (attached).

- Additional notes:
  * We maintain tenant isolation at the storage and logical layers; no co-mingling of PII across tenants.
  * For high-sensitivity workloads we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with BYOK + storage restrictions.
  * We support export of tenant data in standard JSON/NDJSON via the Admin API; exported data requests are fulfilled within 48 hours for standard SOWs.

Attachments: NSI_HostedAPI_Answers_20261123.pdf, Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_Q3_2026.pdf, data_flow_diagram_nshore.png

Next steps: if the above aligns, Monica (legal) — can you [1] confirm the backup purge window we should propose in the DPA (90 days is default) and [2] confirm whether we can commit to a 48-hour primary purge SLA? Laura — please advise if sales wants to offer a reduced-price option for 30-day backup retention.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: North Shore — DPA/retention commit drafts

Team — quick internal thread before we send final to North Shore. Key asks from customer and proposed commitments: 

1) Primary purge SLA: customer asked for explicit timeline. I propose we commit to purging marked objects from primary storage within 48 hours (business). We should caveat business hours and maintenance windows. Monica, OK to promise 48h in DPA?

2) Backup purge: they want assurance backups won’t keep data indefinitely. Default is 90 days; legal please advise whether we can offer 30 days as a negotiated term for NSI without large infra changes. If we shorten to 30 days we should add a 30-day operational notice for restore capability and a small SLA credit.

3) Legal hold: process described below; hold pauses automated deletion but not offline cold-archive until release. Monica, please draft a short hold-process clause we can attach to the DPA.

4) BYOK note: for their high-sensitivity lines, recommend Private (BYOK). Sales: if they request BYOK in Hosted we must move to Dedicated or Private; Laura, can you confirm pricing impact?

I attached a draft one-page summary we can send to Karen. If Monica signs off I’ll send final to Karen and copy legal.

—R

(Attachment: NSI_DPA_Retention_Draft_v1.pdf)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Lopez <karen.lopez@northshoreins.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire — Hosted API commitments and artifacts

Karen —

Following internal review, please find our firmed commitments for North Shore (summary attached and copies of SOC2 + diagram linked):

- Residency: Production tenant data will be pinned to US-East (N. Virginia) and US-West (Oregon). No replication outside the US unless North Shore instructs otherwise in writing.

- Primary purge SLA: Redwood commits to removing customer-marked objects from primary storage within 48 hours (business hours). Emergency requests can be escalated via support and handled on an accelerated timeline.

- Backup purge: Standard backup rotation is 90 days. We will include an option in the DPA to reduce backup retention to 30 days for North Shore; please note this requires a mutual operational agreement and a small service-level credit. Monica has prepared proposed DPA wording and will provide the clause for your counsel.

- Legal hold: Preservation holds are supported; a written request to our legal channel is required. While a hold is active, automatic deletions are paused for the specified objects. Holds are logged in the audit trail and exported on request.

- Evidence: SOC2 Type II Q3 2026 (link) and a data-flow diagram are available here: https://drive.redwood.com/reports/SOC2-Q3-2026 and (see attached data_flow_diagram_nshore.png).

Next steps:
1) Monica will share a short DPA amendment clause for backup retention and legal-hold language (copying this thread).
2) If North Shore wants the 30-day backup option, Laura will produce the pricing addendum.
3) We can set a 30-minute call next week to walk your security team through the diagram and the purge workflows.

Let me know which time slots work. Thanks again for the clear questions — happy to get these written into the DPA so procurement can close.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
